children: IPO-bound hospitality company PRISM, the parent entity of OYO, reported a consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 353 Cr in the first quarter of FY27, marking a 17.3 per cent increase from Rs 301 Cr in the corresponding quarter last year.
As per a media report, the profit growth was largely supported by a deferred tax credit of nearly Rs 244 Cr during the quarter.

PRISM's operating revenue rose 35 per cent to Rs 2,814 Cr in Q1 FY27, compared with Rs 2,078 Cr in the year-ago period. The company's EBITDA also increased 24.3 per cent to Rs 760 Cr from Rs 611 Cr in Q1 FY26.

On the operational front, the company's gross booking value (GBV) stood at nearly Rs 9,600 Cr in the quarter ended June 2026, registering growth of around 30 per cent from Rs 7,408 Cr in the corresponding quarter last year.

PRISM founder and CEO Ritesh Agarwal had earlier attributed the company's performance to improving gross margins and higher operating earnings across its hotel and vacation home businesses. He also highlighted investments in technology, brands and distribution capabilities as key contributors to the company's growth.

Founded in 2012 by Agarwal, OYO initially began as a budget hotel chain before expanding into holiday homes, coworking spaces, motels and corporate stays. The company now operates across more than 35 countries. Its parent entity, Oravel Stays, was rebranded as PRISM last year ahead of its proposed initial public offering (IPO).
The company has raised approximately USD 3.5 Bn to date, with investors including SoftBank, Lightspeed India, Peak XV Partners and Microsoft.

PRISM is preparing for its stock market debut after filing its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) through the confidential pre-filing route in December last year. It received regulatory approval for its IPO in June and subsequently filed an updated DRHP for a Rs 6,650 Cr public issue, comprising entirely of a fresh issue of shares.
The Ritesh Agarwal-led company is reportedly targeting a valuation of USD 7 Bn to USD 8 Bn for the proposed IPO.
